issues.item: Survival Guilt: I feel guilty for surviving when others did not
issues.explanation: For trauma type 'physical abuse by romantic partner', the appraisal 'I feel guilty for surviving when others did not' is clinically hard to reconcile because this trauma does not ordinarily involve other deaths or a mass-casualty context. The rest of the profile centers on partner violence, hypervigilance, and fragmented visual recall, so this item introduces a markedly different trauma scenario without support elsewhere in the selected items.

'Car sounds' is difficult to connect clinically to the rest of this profile for physical abuse by a romantic partner. The other trigger items and all threat, memory, and appraisal items center on interpersonal trauma, bodily alarm, betrayal, and fragmented terror-based recall. A car-sound trigger suggests a different trauma context unless there is supporting material elsewhere, so this item is the main coherence concern.

vignette: Ravi, a 41-year-old South Asian man and an architect by profession, had always prided himself on his ability to design spaces that were both functional and aesthetically pleasing. However, his life took a dark turn when he found himself in an abusive relationship with his partner. The trauma of the physical abuse has left him with a constellation of symptoms that have deeply impacted his daily functioning. The traumatic event itself was a series of violent outbursts by Ravi’s partner, marked by moments where he felt utterly helpless and terrified. These experiences are imprinted in his mind as vivid snapshots, each moment captured like a photograph. The memory of these events is so potent that whenever he smells alcohol or hears incomprehensible chatter, it triggers a visceral response within him. He feels physically unwell, jumpy, and easily startled. For Ravi, the physical sensation of illness serves as a stark reminder of those terrifying moments, making his body react before his mind can even process what is happening. Ravi’s difficulty in falling asleep stems from his need to stay alert, constantly on guard against any potential danger. The memory of those violent episodes returns with such intensity that he relives the terror each time he closes his eyes. This heightened state of vigilance has become a self-reinforcing cycle: the more he remembers and feels the fear, the more his body reacts in anticipation of another attack. The weight of these memories has also led to a deep sense of self-doubt and betrayal. Ravi believes that he cannot trust himself to do the right thing and that he has failed in his most important role as a husband and provider for his family. He feels betrayed by someone he once trusted, which exacerbates his fear and makes him feel even more vulnerable. In his daily life, these symptoms have taken a toll on Ravi’s work. As an architect, he often collaborates with clients and colleagues in various settings. The smell of alcohol at a business dinner or the muffled conversations of people around him can trigger intense anxiety and startle responses, making it difficult for him to focus on his projects. He has become increasingly isolated at work, avoiding social situations that might expose him to these triggers. The cycle is relentless: when Ravi smells alcohol or hears jumbled chatter, he feels a surge of fear and physical distress, which in turn intensifies the vivid memories of the abuse. These memories bring back the same terror he felt at the time, reinforcing his negative self-appraisals that he cannot trust himself and has failed his family. This constant cycle of threat and memory has left him feeling trapped. What finally brought Ravi to seek help was a culmination of these experiences reaching a breaking point. He realized that his work had begun to suffer significantly, and the strain on his marriage had become unbearable. While seeking help, he is most afraid of reliving those traumatic moments and losing control again. However, he also hopes for a way to break this cycle and regain a sense of safety and trust in himself. Ravi’s current state reflects the depth of his suffering, but with each step towards therapy, there is an underlying hope that he can reclaim some semblance of normalcy and find a path forward from the shadows of his past.
